title: BOAgents Slice (Settings + BoBots + Telemetry)
markdown:
The **bo** module (`openexecutive.bo`) is the BOAgents product slice shipped in Valul 1: a self-contained, separable surface with its own SQLite database (`bo_agents.db`, override `BOAGENTS_DB_PATH`) so the product can split from the host app later without a data migration.

**Identity and tenancy.** `bo/identity.py` resolves every `/bo/*` request to an `Identity {actor, tenant, role}`. The tenant comes from `BO_TENANT_ID` (server config) — never from the request body or a picker; a caller that asserts a different tenant via `x-bo-tenant` or `?tenant=` is refused 403 without learning the configured value. Roles: `viewer` (any authenticated email) < `operator` (shared-secret service identity, can simulate) < `admin` (`BO_ADMIN_EMAILS` or a roster principal). On a public deployment (`OE_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT`) an unauthenticated request is refused — the dev fallback only exists when the deployment is not public.

**Settings (BO-SET-001).** Thirty-five registered keys live in `bo/settings/registry.py` — the nine original ones plus the eleven `bo.router.*` controls (observe_enabled, eligibility/policy lists, min_quality, eval_max_age_days, max_estimated_cost, observation_retention_days, delivery_interval_s, delivery_batch_size, delivery_max_attempts) — display name, language (`ro`/`en`), IANA timezone, simulation step limit, simulation retention days, plus the four VAL2-01 package controls and the fifteen `bo.exec.*` execution controls (`enabled`, `guardian_endpoint`, `guardian_secret_ref`, `guardian_auth_required`, `guardian_policy_secret_ref`, `guardian_timeout_s`, `max_delegation_depth`, `max_steps`, `max_effect_attempts`, `lease_seconds`, `default_concurrency`, `checkpoint_required`, `budget_cap`, `retry_backoff_s`, `retention_days`) (`bo.packages.enabled` — off by default, `bo.packages.max_package_bytes`, `bo.packages.trust_store_json`, `bo.packages.rollback_requires_approval`). Each key is a typed contract: explicit validator, apply mode (`IMMEDIATE` | `NEW_RUN`), edit role, Romanian labels/help, and sensitivity class. `bo/settings/store.py` persists one row per `(tenant, key)` with a monotonically increasing `version`; every write carries `expected_version` and a stale writer gets a deterministic 409 (CAS inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`). Reads always report `value` + `origin` (`tenant` | `default`) + `version`, so the UI can never confuse configured with factory. Writes audit via `log_event` (`bo_setting_change`) with old/new values — no sensitive keys exist in this slice.

**BoBots (BO-BOT-001/002/003).** A BoBot is a deterministic automation: event → typed conditions → plan → controls → authorized effect → receipt. `bo/bots/models.py` is a closed-world pydantic grammar (`extra="forbid"`): trigger, optional top-level predicate, steps of type `check | emit_finding | set_field | notify | note`. `bo/bots/predicates.py` is a three-valued evaluator (`TRUE | FALSE | UNKNOWN`) over `eq ne in exists lt lte gt gte` plus bounded `all/any/not` — a missing input is UNKNOWN, never a coerced false, and UNKNOWN gates the plan rather than letting it through. No eval, SQL, or shell: the grammar is the whole language.

**Lifecycle.** Drafts carry a `draft_version` CAS counter; publish copies the draft into an immutable `published` version row and flips `active_version_no` atomically, then opens the next draft as a copy — editing a draft can never mutate the active version. Runs snapshot `version_hash` + `config_version` + a config snapshot, so a simulation is reproducible forever: same input + same version ⇒ same `plan_hash` (SHA-256 over canonical plan).

**Simulation is the only executor in Valul 1.** `bo/bots/service.py::simulate` walks steps against a caller-supplied synthetic context, records a per-step timeline (`SIMULATED | SKIPPED`), collects findings, and writes receipts marked `NOT_EXECUTED`. There is no code path to a provider, the network, email, or an external effect. The `bo.bobot.simulation.max_steps` setting caps evaluated steps (`PARTIAL` when hit); `retention_days` drives a sweep that deletes expired `kind='simulation'` runs (cascading their timeline) — audit rows are never in scope. The shipped example (`heartbeat_stale.bobot.json`) turns a stale heartbeat into a simulated finding.

**Telemetry (BO-TEL-001).** `bo/telemetry/` implements the shared `bo.telemetry.v1` envelope: strict, closed validation (`schema.py`, mirrored by `fixtures/bo/telemetry/bo.telemetry.v1.schema.json`), plus an injectable adapter (`adapter.py`) that is **disabled by default** — `emit()` drops before building the envelope unless `BO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` is set. Transports: `NullTransport`, `BufferedTransport` (tests/dev), `HttpTransport` (POST to a Guardian-compatible endpoint, only when explicitly configured). Identity fields (`tenantRef`, `product`, `producerId`, `installationId`) are stamped by the adapter from the authenticated tenant + deployment config — never trusted from caller payloads. Default payloads carry no prompts, documents, secrets, or personal data; the schema rejects unknown and denied fields outright.

**Signed packages (bo.package.v1, VAL2-01).** `bo/packages/` implements the shared signed-package contract: `contract.py` validates the manifest shape and enforces read limits *before and during* file reads; `canon.py` is the BO-C14N-v1 canonicalization (sorted keys, UTF-8, no floats — JSON with duplicate keys or NaN/Infinity is rejected before signature checks); `verify.py` runs the nine contract steps fail-fast and returns the shared `Verdict` shape; `registry.py` is the tenant trust store (`bo.package.registry.v1`) — **the public key is never trusted from the manifest**, it resolves only through publisher/keyId in the registry, with revocation and expiry. `service.py` runs import → verify → quarantine: accepted bytes are copied under their artifact-set digest (re-hashed while copying — drift between verify and copy is `ARTIFACT_DRIFT`), lifecycle is QUARANTINED → DRAFT (promotion re-verifies the stored copy), rejected imports are persisted with their verdict for audit. Same version + same artifact-set digest is an idempotent reimport; same version + different digest is `VERSION_CONFLICT`; downgrade requires a tenant-bound, digest-bound, version-bound, expiring single-use approval (`bo_package_approvals`). Nothing is ever activated — there is no execution path in this lot.

**Observe-mode router (VAL3-01 + REM-01).** `bo/routing/` is the observe-only
model router: an administered per-tenant catalog (provider/model/version,
capabilities, regions, cost and quality evidence — decimal-string money, a
missing quality score means *never evaluated*, not zero), a pure
deterministic engine (eligibility filters in fixed order — provider → region
→ capabilities → budget → availability → eval freshness — *before* scoring,
then score desc → cost asc → identity asc tie-break), and durable
observations. `observe.py` hooks `audit.usage.log_model_usage` post-call:
computes what the administered catalog would have recommended vs the model
actually used, persists both separately, and stops — the hook performs zero
network I/O. Delivery is a separate bounded mechanism (`delivery.py`): the
complete `bo.model-observation.v1` envelope (stable `eventId` + server-derived
identity) lands in `bo_telemetry_outbox` *before* the first send attempt and
is re-sent byte-identically on every retry — a lost ACK surfaces receiver-side
as DUPLICATE, never a second logical observation. Claims are leased under
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (concurrent flushes cannot double-send), bounded by
`delivery_batch_size`, drained by an optional daemon worker every
`delivery_interval_s` seconds (0 = `POST /bo/routing/flush` only), and
envelopes past `delivery_max_attempts` are dead-lettered — visible in
`/bo/routing/status`, never silently dropped. The router NEVER changes the
real route, never blocks a call, never calls a provider; with
`bo.router.observe_enabled=false` (default) it is a no-op, and `bo.bots`
imports nothing from `bo.routing` — BoBots keep zero LLM dependency.

**Delegated execution (VAL4-01 + REM-01).** `bo/execution/` is the
limited delegated-execution engine — disabled by default
(`bo.exec.enabled=false`). Mandates (`mandate.py`) form a strict
intersection chain: a child ⊆ parent ∩ tenant caps, never amplified, and
the principal ref is always the server-derived creator. `store.py` owns
the atomic machinery: budget+concurrency reservations under
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, run leases with `lease_seq` fencing (a stale worker
cannot finalize), and the effect ledger — one row per
`{run}:{step}` intent with idempotencyKey, payloadDigest, provider,
status, receiptRef. `engine.py` enforces a fixed step order: flags →
mandate-chain re-check → mandatory checkpoint → ledger intent → effect
under lease+fence. Ambiguous provider outcomes become `UNKNOWN`
(idempotent, resumable) or `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` (non-idempotent —
a blind retry could double the effect; only an audited `mark_failed` or
a found provider receipt unblocks it). Cancellation never reverses a
completed effect.

**Synthetic pilot (VAL5).** `bo/pilot/` is the bounded diagnostic pilot: a
signed `bo.package.v1` import is verified, approved, activated (CAS), then
`service.submit` drives exactly one `diagnose` step against the allowlisted
loopback service (`fixture.py`) through the normal engine. `provider.py`
treats the correlated HTTP receipt as the authority for the external
effect — the persisted observation envelope (`bo_pilot_observations`) and
the derived outbox envelopes are evidence-adjacent, never a veto: a
telemetry outage marks the ledger receipt `telemetryStatus: DEGRADED`
(+ `telemetryError` stage code) while the run stays `SUCCEEDED`, and a
missing/corrupt/foreign receipt still lands `UNKNOWN`. `service.status`
reports a per-run `telemetry` posture (expected/queued/delivered/dead/
missing/replayable) read straight from `bo_telemetry_outbox`, so a
half-persisted envelope set is visibly `degraded` instead of silently
lost; an authorized `replay_telemetry` (`execution:write`, audited)
re-enqueues only the missing eventIds from the persisted observation —
idempotent, no provider call, no new effect, dead-lettered rows keep
their operator-retry history. Warnings across the telemetry-adjacent
paths log only the exception class, never `exc_info` or raw messages.

**Guardian linkage (REM-01).** `guardian.py` is the authority boundary:
when `bo.exec.guardian_endpoint` is set, every effectful step re-reads
`GET /v1/mandates/{guardian_ref}/status` live — REVOKED/EXPIRED/404
deny the effect, transport failure pauses the run (recoverable), and
`bo.exec.guardian_auth_required=true` makes a missing binding or
credential deny outright. A bound mandate never degrades to
standalone: missing endpoint or credential pauses the run
(`guardian_unavailable`), and a malformed authority response is a
denial (`guardian_invalid_response`). With the optional
`bo.exec.guardian_policy_secret_ref` credential (`execpolicy:read`
scope) each effect boundary also re-reads `GET /v1/exec-policies` —
a revoked current policy denies as `policy_revoked` even while the
mandate itself stays ACTIVE, and an action/resource dropped from the
policy denies as `outside_policy`. The token comes only from the env var named by
`bo.exec.guardian_secret_ref`. Evidence rides the same durable outbox as
routing (`kind="execution"`) but on the `bo.execution-control.event.v1`
contract: one envelope = exactly one `checkpoint` (execution state,
never effect proof — CLAIMED and terminal states carry the lease's
fencingToken so the receiver can order epochs) or `receipt` (the ledger
evidence: intentRef, idempotencyKey, payloadDigest, status, receiptRef).
`delivery.py` routes execution envelopes to Guardian's real
`/v1/execution-events` with the execution credential: RECEIVED/DUPLICATE
count as delivered, 401/403/409/413/422 dead-letter visibly
(non-transient — identical retries can never succeed), receiver-down and
5xx stay pending, and provisional `bo.execution-control.v1` envelopes
dead-letter with a re-emission hint instead of retrying forever.

**HTTP surface** (`api/routes/bo.py`, prefix `/bo`): `GET/PUT /bo/settings/{key}`, `GET/POST /bo/bots`, `POST /bo/bots/example`, `GET/PATCH /bo/bots/{id}`, `POST /bo/bots/{id}/publish`, `POST /bo/bots/{id}/simulate`, `GET /bo/bots/{id}/runs`, `GET /bo/runs/{id}` (step timeline), `GET /bo/telemetry/status`, `POST /bo/telemetry/validate` (schema gate), `GET /bo/packages`, `POST /bo/packages/import`, `GET /bo/packages/{import_id}`, `POST /bo/packages/{import_id}/promote`, `GET/POST /bo/packages-approvals`, `POST /bo/packages-approvals/{id}/revoke`, `GET/POST /bo/routing/catalog`, `PUT /bo/routing/catalog/{id}`, `GET /bo/routing/observations`, `GET /bo/routing/observations/{id}`, `GET /bo/routing/status`, `POST /bo/routing/flush`, `GET/POST /bo/execution/mandates`, `POST /bo/execution/mandates/{id}/revoke`, `GET/POST /bo/execution/runs`, `GET /bo/execution/runs/{id}`, `POST /bo/execution/runs/{id}/pause`, `POST /bo/execution/runs/{id}/resume`, `POST /bo/execution/runs/{id}/cancel`, `POST /bo/execution/runs/{id}/reconcile`, `POST /bo/execution/work`, `GET /bo/execution/status`, `GET /bo/execution/outbox`, `POST /bo/execution/outbox/{id}/retry` (audited requeue with an operator reason), `POST /bo/execution/runs/{id}/verify-authority`, `GET /bo/pilot`, `PUT /bo/pilot/activation`, `POST /bo/pilot/runs`, `POST /bo/pilot/runs/{id}/telemetry/replay` (live re-check of the run's Guardian binding, returning the effective authority or the blocking reason). Pause and cancel take a required `reason`, audited on the run; cancel never reverses completed effects. Domain errors map centrally via `register_error_handlers`: unknown→404, CAS/state→409, validation→422 (`package_rejected` carries the verifier code), identity→401/403.
